summary.title: Check these fields before you send:

status.failed: The form could not be sent. Try again later.
status.rateLimit: Too many submissions. Try again in a moment.
status.token: The form could not be checked. Wait a moment and send it again.
status.turnstile: The check against robots failed. Try again.
status.unavailable: This form is not available now.
status.tooLarge: The form is too large to send.

errors.option: Choose one of the options for {label}.
errors.unknown: {label} is not a field of this form.
errors.noSecret: The site has no signing secret for forms.
errors.noStore: The site has no store for form submissions yet.

admin.title: Submissions
admin.intro: What visitors sent through the forms of the site.
admin.noAccess: You do not have access to the submissions.
admin.emptyHint: Make a form in the Forms section, or define one in code.
admin.noStoreHint: The site needs a store before a form can take submissions. The setup page shows the steps.

settings.title: Forms
settings.intro: A form needs a place to keep its submissions, a secret to sign its token, and an email setup to tell you about each one. Cloudflare Turnstile is optional.

store.title: Store for submissions
store.why: Submissions hold personal data, so they never go in the Git repository. They go in a store that you choose.
store.missingMount: The setting names the storage "{name}", but the site does not define it.
store.devHint: In development the submissions go in the folder .data/pluto-forms. A site in production needs a real store.

vercel.name: Vercel
vercel.step1: In the Vercel dashboard, open the Storage tab of the project and add Upstash Redis from the Marketplace.
vercel.step2: Check that the project has the variables UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL and UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN. The integration adds them.

netlify.name: Netlify
netlify.step1: Netlify Blobs is part of every Netlify site. You do not need to create anything.
netlify.step2: Do nothing here. The next step gives the name of the store.

cloudflare.name: Cloudflare
cloudflare.step1: In the Cloudflare dashboard, open Storage and databases, then KV, and create a namespace called forms.
cloudflare.step2: Open your Pages or Workers project, then Settings, then Bindings, and add a KV binding named FORMS for that namespace.

server.name: My own server
server.step1: Pick a folder that the server keeps between deploys, for example /var/lib/my-site/forms.
server.step2: Make sure that the user of the site can write to it. Use that folder as the base in the next step.

secret.title: Signing secret
secret.why: The form gets a signed token when it loads. A robot that sends the form at once has no valid token.
secret.fromGithub: The site uses a key made from the session password of the CMS. Nothing to do.
secret.set: Set the variable NUXT_PLUTO_FORMS_SECRET in the settings of your host to a long random text, and deploy again.

turnstile.title: Cloudflare Turnstile
turnstile.why: The built-in checks (a hidden field, a minimum fill time and a rate limit) stop most robots. Turnstile adds a check from Cloudflare. It is free and has no puzzles for most visitors.
turnstile.half: Only one of the two Turnstile variables is set. Set both, or Turnstile stays off.
turnstile.step1: In the Cloudflare dashboard, open Turnstile and add a widget for the domain of the site.
turnstile.step2: Copy the site key to the variable NUXT_PLUTO_FORMS_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY in the settings of your host.
turnstile.step3: Copy the secret key to the variable NUXT_PLUTO_FORMS_TURNSTILE_SECRET, and deploy again.

mail.title: Email
mail.why: The form sends an email to the addresses of the form for each submission.
mail.logOnly: Emails only show in the server log, because email is in development mode.
mail.none: The site has no email provider. Submissions are stored, but nobody gets an email.

form.label: Form
form.description: A form for the site: fields, who gets the email, and what the visitor sees after sending. A page shows it with the form block.

slug.label: Handle
slug.description: The name that a page uses to find the form, for example contact.

recipients.label: Send the email to
recipients.description: One address, or more separated by commas. Empty: no email, the submissions stay in the store.

redirect.label: Open this page after sending
redirect.description: A path (/thanks) or a URL. Empty: show the message.

retentionDays.label: Keep submissions (days)
retentionDays.description: The store deletes older submissions. 0 keeps them for ever.
